title: The Tenants’ Petition
sceneText:
You are in the office when they come.

Five of them. They stand in the courtyard and wait for somebody to come out. At the head of them is a man in his sixties, Old Wendt, whom you have seen twice out in the fields. He has a sheet of paper in his hand.

On the paper are the names of five households, and below them five signatures, three of which are marks.

“Roofs and a cow shed,” Old Wendt says. “It was reported last year. Mr Hartmann wrote it down. It should be in the book.”

There is no grievance in the way he says it. He is stating a fact he has already checked.

You go back to the office and look through the outstanding list, and you find it. It is there, dated last November. Neat hand. Nothing recorded after it.

variants.informed:
You know that the five households are not in the same position.

Old Wendt’s roof has leaked for two years, but there are only two of them in the house and one room is still fit to live in.

The one by the mill is the common cow shed, with one corner down, so that the whole village’s cattle are packed into the half that is left. Sickness in cattle spreads.

One is an old woman living alone. Her house will in fact stand another winter, but not two.

The remaining two have the least damage and the most people in them.
variants.uninformed: There are five names on the list. You do not know which household is worst off.
variants.partial_fair:
You say which three will be done, and why.

Nobody objects. Old Wendt nods and says the cow shed is certainly the most pressing. One of the men from the other two households opens his mouth, and in the end says nothing.

“And the rest?” Old Wendt asks.

You say after the harvest.

“Right,” he says. “Only keep it in mind.”

He leaves the paper behind, on the stone ledge of the porch.
variants.partial_unfair:
You say which three will be done.

For a moment nobody speaks.

Then Old Wendt says right, thank you. He says it more politely than he said anything before.

After they have gone the paper is still on the stone ledge of the porch, until the wind takes it to the ground.

effects.logEntry: You approved repairs for all five households.

choices.resultText:
Old Wendt takes the paper back, folds it twice and puts it in his pocket.

“Thank you,” he says. And then they go, without staying about.

That afternoon Martha says less in the kitchen than usual. Going past, you find her talking to two others, and she stops when she sees you.

The last half of what you hear is “… somebody finally.”

choices.text: Do the three that cannot wait

effects.logEntry: You chose three households to do first.

choices.text: After this year’s harvest is in

effects.logEntry: You put the petition off until after the harvest.

choices.resultText:
Old Wendt looks at you a while.

“Right,” he says.

He folds the paper up and puts it away, and turns and goes. The other four follow him. Through all of it not one of them says anything more.

The kitchen light went out earlier than usual that night.
